# thresholdr <a href="https://thresholdr.r-dcm.org"><img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="thresholdr website" /></a>

<!-- badges: start -->

[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/thresholdr)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=thresholdr)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/r-dcm/thresholdr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/r-dcm/thresholdr/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

The goal of thresholdr is to estimate optimal probability thresholds for determining classifications when the true state is unknown, such as when using diagnostic classification models.

## Installation

You can install the development version of thresholdr like so:

``` r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("r-dcm/thresholdr")
```

## Example usage

When the true classifications are known, we can calculate the optimal threshold directly using a supported method, such as Youden's J statistic.
For example, `dcm_probs` contains estimated probabilities of proficiency from a simulated diagnostic classification model, along with the true classifications:

```{r example}
library(thresholdr)

calc_youden(estimates = dcm_probs$att1$estimate, truth = dcm_probs$att1$truth)
```

In practice, however, the true classifications are unknown.
Instead, we can estimate the optimal threshold from the probabilities alone, for example by resampling, and compare it to the traditional threshold of 0.5:

```{r resample}
set.seed(1213)
optimal_resample(
  estimates = dcm_probs$att1$estimate,
  optimal_method = "youden",
  comp_thresholds = 0.5
)
```

To estimate thresholds for every attribute in a model fitted with `{measr}`, `{GDINA}`, or `{CDM}`, use `find_threshold()`.
For a complete walk-through, see the `vignette("thresholdr")` article.
